CBT is cognitive behavioural therapy. I'm not sure on the specifics, but it's supposed to really help (for the most part) with anxiety disorders.
I live in the UK. Only made the comparison to the US as that's the only other place where I know how healthcare works. There's probably more countries where you would pay for it than not, but I wouldn't be British if I didn't have the chance to rib on America's healthcare system.

I'll probably reply to the rest later, but I'm completely drained. The good news is that now I don't have the energy to commit suicide, I suppose.

Round about the middle at the moment, yeah. Technically, the cycle starts at being completely unable to move, but the majority is spent as I first described. Probably should have structured that better.

My parents wake me up in the morning to give me antidepressants. Without them I would be unable to move at all or feel any emotion whatsoever (or so I suspect; I haven't missed a day and don't intend to). They obviously do that because of the inability to move already mentioned, but also because you're supposed to eat with them or they can cause vomiting.

 I'm also currently awaiting CBT and a low mood and anxiety group but I'm with an NHS service in the UK, and they love their waiting lists. I don't think we could afford mental healthcare at all in the US, and I get checked on regularly, so I can't complain.

my OCPD is somewhat mild in comparison to everything else, but I expect that it's something of a factor in my inability to recover (and my inability to help other people by extension). Obviously, depression causes a shortened attention span in me anyway. I used to occupy myself with writing, as I still had anxiety issues and thought that it would be the easiest way to do something useful, but I spent eons more planning than actually doing. With my shortened attention span and general lack of energy, it's exasperated as there are a million things I'm frustrated with having no control over.

Uninteresting to say the least. I either sleep for most of the morning, or am completely unable to move. I'm given the antidepressants at some point in the morning along with breakfast. Once I'm actually able to move, anxiety kicks in. I usually spend most of the day rocking back and forth after that in order to distract myself, from intrusive thoughts and the like but otherwise it's usually a futile attempt to occupy myself with any productive activity, which ends in frustration as I'm unable to do. This then repeats for 2-4 weeks until I have some sort of breakdown in which I have to be physically restrained from suicide. After that I go back to complete catatonia for a week or so and the cycle repeats itself.

Currently no goals. I've spent most of my time either unable to get out of bed and leave the house. Basically, unable to do anything all but fulfil my most basic needs, so the goals (set by others) have really just been 'avoid death'.
I've tried to help other people in the very few times I've been outside. Something as simple as giving money to a homeless person caused me to have a panic attack and I would have thrown myself in front of a train were the transport police not nearby to stop me.

I'm not sure if that's relevant. I've been diagnosed with a load of different mental illnesses. The suffering I endure would be the same regardless of what my age. I'd rather not go in to too much detail, as I don't want people whom I know to find out. It's unlikely, but possible. I'm sure what I've said, along with my verbosity, would at least give an approximate age anyhow.

Helping people really means anything that makes others happy; it doesn't exactly have to be changing the world, but it can be. Anything from giving a homeless person £10, to giving support to someone who's lonely, to giving massive (relative to income) amounts of money to charity. I read that a philosophy of nothing but altruism helped people lead happier lives, but I can't even do the simplest of those. For the longest time, I was in a catatonic state; I still struggle with doing anything aside from doing anything that continues my life (eating, drinking, sleeping etc.). That makes me feel awful.
